subject: general
question: The Government of India Act, 1919, which contained several reforms, was passed on the basis of which of the following reports/reforms?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Montagu–Chelmsford Reforms**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Government of India Act, 1919, also known as the Montagu–Chelmsford Reforms, was a significant constitutional reform enacted by the British Parliament.
 
• It introduced the concept of dyarchy, which divided the subjects of administration into two categories: transferred and reserved.
 
• The Act proposed a dual form of government for the major provinces, with elected Indian ministers accountable to the provincial legislatures.
 
• It also expanded the participation of Indians in the governance of British India by allowing a greater number of Indians to be elected to the central and provincial legislative councils.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Morley-Minto Reforms (Indian Councils Act 1909)**

 
 
• The Morley-Minto Reforms were introduced in 1909 to expand the Indian legislative councils at both the central and provincial levels.
 
• It allowed for a limited increase in the number of Indian members in the legislative councils.
 
• The reforms also introduced separate electorates for Muslims, which was a significant step towards communal representation in Indian politics.
 
 
 
• **Electoral Reform**
 
 
• Electoral reforms generally refer to changes in electoral systems to improve how public desires are expressed in election results.
 
• In the context of Indian history, electoral reforms have included measures such as the introduction of universal adult suffrage, the establishment of the Election Commission of India, and measures to ensure free and fair elections.
 
 
 
• **Dyarchy**
 
 
• Dyarchy was a system of dual government introduced by the Government of India Act, 1919.
 
• Under dyarchy, certain areas of government (the "transferred" subjects) were placed under the control of Indian ministers responsible to the legislature, while others (the "reserved" subjects) remained under the control of the British governor and his executive council.
 
• This system was intended to gradually introduce Indians to self-governance, although it was criticized for being overly complex and for not giving Indians enough real power.
 
 
 
• **Legislative Councils**
 
 
• The legislative councils were bodies at both the central and provincial levels in British India that had advisory and legislative functions.
 
• Over time, reforms such as the Indian Councils Act of 1892, the Morley-Minto Reforms, and the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms expanded their size and the role of elected Indian members.
 
• These councils were a key part of the British strategy to involve Indians in governance while maintaining ultimate control.
